1.assumed: All EM waves are transverse, travel at c in a vacuum and can be polarised.

2.assumed: Light bends towards the normal entering glass and away from it on leaving.

3.assumed: Work done stretching is the area under the force–extension graph.

4.assumed: Resultant of two forces lies between their difference (opposite) and their sum (same direction).

5.assumed: With no horizontal force, horizontal velocity of a projectile stays constant.

6.assumed: Impulse equals change of momentum, so impulse divided by mass gives final speed from rest.

7.assumed: A couple is a pair of equal, opposite, parallel forces not acting along the same line.

8.assumed: Scaling both resistances by the same fraction scales the parallel total by that fraction too.

9.assumed: Less light raises LDR resistance, so circuit current and the fixed resistor's p.d. both fall.

10.assumed: At striking voltage the electron energy eV equals photon energy hc/λ.

11.assumed: Find mass from weight/g; tension = weight + ma.

12.assumed: Total power is the sum of lamp powers; I = P/V.

13.assumed: Energy lost to resistance = Ep − Ek; force = energy lost ÷ distance along the slope.

14.assumed: Kinetic energy eV = p²/2m so p ∝ √V and λ = h/p ∝ 1/√V.

15.assumed: Stationary means equilibrium; upthrust plus any support balances weight; here upthrust equals weight.

16.assumed: Power = intensity × area (mm² to m²); energy = power × time.

17.assumed: A force perpendicular to the displacement does no work.

18.assumed: Combine series resistors by adding and parallel ones by reciprocals, step by step.

19.assumed: A car's mass is about 1000 kg, so momentum ≈ 10⁴ kg m s⁻¹.

20.assumed: SI base units include kg, m, s, A, K, mol; the coulomb is derived (A s).

21(a).assumed: Ek = ½mv² with mass converted from g to kg.

21(b).assumed: Velocity is the gradient of a displacement–time graph; flat line means stationary.

21(c).assumed: Read stopping distance or time from the graph, then apply suvat with final velocity zero.

22(a).assumed: Weight of a uniform platform acts at its midpoint; take moments about the wall pivot.

22(b).assumed: Strain = stress/E, then compression = strain × original length.

23(a).assumed: Momentum is conserved only for the whole system; the Earth gains equal and opposite momentum.

23(b)(i).assumed: Force equals gradient of the momentum–time graph: change of momentum over time.

23(b)(ii).assumed: Total momentum stays constant, so Y gains exactly what X loses over the same interval.

24(a)(i).assumed: Find current from V/R, then v = I/(Ane).

24(a)(ii).assumed: Hot NTC thermistor has lower resistance so current rises; ideal supply keeps terminal p.d. constant.

24(b)(i).assumed: Contact at midpoint gives half the wire's resistance; current = V/R; then ε = V + Ir.

24(b)(ii).assumed: More external resistance means less current, smaller lost volts Ir, so terminal p.d. rises.

25(a)(i).assumed: Wavelength is the distance between adjacent crests on a displacement–distance graph.

25(a)(ii).assumed: Energy spreads over a larger area so amplitude falls; intensity ∝ amplitude².

25(b)(i).assumed: Interference is the superposition of coherent waves.

25(b)(ii).assumed: Path difference of a half-integer number of wavelengths gives destructive interference.

26(a).assumed: Express newtons as kg m s⁻²; simplify base units to m s⁻¹.

26(b).assumed: Measure mass on a balance and length with a ruler; μ = m/L; improve resolution and repeat.

26(c).assumed: Speed fixed by tension; λ ∝ 1/f; loops are half wavelengths, so L = nλ/2.

27(a).assumed: Threshold frequency is the minimum frequency of radiation that releases electrons from the surface.

27(b)(i).assumed: At the threshold frequency the electrons have zero kinetic energy.

27(b)(ii).assumed: Plot points accurately and draw a ruled line of best fit.

27(b)(iii).assumed: Gradient of φ against f0 is h; convert eV to joules first.

27(b)(iv).assumed: Draw a worst acceptable line; percentage uncertainty = difference in gradient ÷ best gradient × 100.
